brief: JPMorgan's Market Intelligence desk reports APAC equities and US and EU futures lower, with yields and oil in charge. It lists the debated bond sell-off drivers: geopolitics, global fiscal concerns, crowding out from AI corporate issuance, inflation risk, buyback scepticism, and hawkish repricing of central bank paths, notably the BOJ. On that basis the desk turned tactically cautious or neutral on global equities and took profit on gold, while flagging that muted VIX and downside skew moves sit against low realized volatility. It still expects an attractive Q4 setup, arguing the global manufacturing upturn supports JPM Economics' 3% annualised industrial growth forecast for 2H26, and that Asian positioning falling from the 75th percentile to the 40th, plus resumed EM inflows and Korean corporate buybacks, leaves Asian equities on an upward medium-term path even with near-term caution. Regional preference stays long US and Asia versus Europe, with supercycle themes as core longs and index hedges added. The note also carries an EM monetization menu, a Japan FX view tying quarterly BOJ hikes to a 155 to 165 USD/JPY range, and a positioning wrap on hedge fund de-grossing.
